texts: The cold-threshold wind is a cutting north wind.
The cold-threshold wind comes off the Cold Sea on clear winter nights.
The cold-threshold wind chills standing water quickly.
The cold-threshold wind extinguishes unprotected lanterns.
The cold-threshold wind blows between the first hard frost and the spring equinox.
Salt-bloom in mire-essence slows the burn.
A salt-bloomed lantern survives a cold-threshold night.
An unprepared Cliff Path lantern dies on a cold-threshold night.
The cold-threshold wind does not reach the Northcove.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind is a cutting north wind.

q2_gaps: definite-singular generic subject ("The cold-threshold wind is a cutting north wind"): the instruction set states no rule for when a definite singular NP denotes a KIND (Inheritance on a bare kind symbol) rather than a specific referent (witness + Member) — the definite-description rule says "picks out a specific thing" without saying how to tell, and only the "the dodo is extinct" KindProperty example touches the definite-generic case
review.notes: Fusing "cutting" into cutting_north_wind is a judgment call against the "incidental description" bar (a dented pail), but the exposed modifier genus (Inheritance cutting_north_wind cutting) preserves the same inheritances either way. Compound handling is otherwise right: genus wind on both compounds, noun-modifier cold_threshold left unexposed, positional north and participial-adjective cutting exposed.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind comes off the Cold Sea on clear winter nights.

q1_issues.issue: The temporal restriction 'on clear winter nights' is dropped entirely — not even the licensed day-part 'night' is carried on Time — so the parse asserts unrestrictedly that the wind comes off the Cold Sea, which is the widening that Core patterns forbids ('a stated restriction ... is never silently dropped').

q2_gaps: a habitual occasion restricted by a modified bare-plural day-part NP ('on clear winter nights'): day-parts are covered as bare Time symbols and periodic wordings as Every/TimesPer, but there is no licensed slot for a season modifier ('winter') or a weather condition ('clear') qualifying the recurring occasion, and no clause for the whenever/ConditionalProperty machinery to consume
review.notes: Everything else is right: definite-singular subject as a typed witness, cold_threshold_wind fused with the head genus only (noun modifier not exposed), Patient for the non-volitional natural-force subject, Source for path 'off', and one Name plus the name-internal kind atom for the Cold Sea.

issues.reason: *Core patterns* states that a stated restriction 'is never silently dropped — omitting it widens the claim', yet the parse's come/Source bundle carries nothing of 'on clear winter nights' (not even the licensed day-part atom (Time sk_come_1 night)), so it asserts unrestrictedly that the wind comes off the Cold Sea.

gaps_confirmed: A habitual occasion restricted by a modified bare-plural day-part NP ('on clear winter nights'): day-parts are bare Time symbols and periodic wordings take Every/TimesPer, but there is no licensed carrier for a season modifier ('winter') or a weather condition ('clear') qualifying the recurring occasion, and no clause for the whenever / ConditionalProperty machinery to consume.
new_gaps: Since 'clear' and 'winter' have no carrier, carrying only the day-part would still leave the claim unqualified on those dimensions — so the instruction set licenses NO compliant form for this sentence and *Core patterns* forces the whole claim to be withheld. A licensed form would need either an occasion-restrictor slot on a habitual event (condition-state plus season on the recurring occasion) or the whenever/Implication machinery extended to consume an NP adjunct rather than a finite clause.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form must carry the occasion restriction — minimally the licensed day-part (Time sk_come_1 night) — but no licensed carrier exists for 'clear' or for the season 'winter' on a habitual occasion, so no fully compliant form is licensed and *Core patterns* requires leaving the claim out and recording the gap rather than emitting the unrestricted event.
adjudication.notes: The rest of the parse is right: the definite singular subject as a typed witness, cold_threshold_wind with head genus only, Patient for the non-volitional natural-force subject, Source for the path 'off', and one Name plus the separate kind atom for the Cold Sea.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind chills standing water quickly.

review.notes: The definite-singular subject correctly reifies an ordinary event rather than a kind relation (the relational-generic trigger needs bare kind NPs on both sides), the noun modifier 'cold-threshold' is left unexposed while the predicable participial 'standing' is, and unmarked present gets no status atom.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind extinguishes unprotected lanterns.

q1_issues.issue: The subject is a definite singular, which the instruction set routes to an ordinary status-less (habitual/dispositional) event, but the parse instead builds a universal Implication ranging over the bare-plural object, asserting that this wind extinguishes every unprotected lantern.

q2_gaps: an adjectivally-restricted bare-plural object in a non-episodic (habitual/dispositional) clause -- 'extinguishes unprotected lanterns': the prescribed bare kind filler for a non-specific object cannot carry the restrictive modifier, and 'unprotected lantern' is incidental description so it does not fuse into a compound kind
review.notes: The compound decomposition (genus `wind`, noun modifier `cold_threshold` correctly left unexposed), `Agent` on an inanimate transitive subject, `Patient` on `extinguish`, and the absence of a QuantifierPhrase companion are all right. The rule shape itself (constant subject plus a Skolem-function event over a quantified range) is a licensed shape, but the instruction set licenses it for an explicit universal, which this bare plural is not.

issues.reason: The rule asserts at strength 0.9 that an arbitrary unprotected lantern anywhere is extinguished by this one wind, which the text does not state — the clause is a status-less habitual/dispositional event on a definite singular subject, and a bare-plural non-specific object's licensed treatment is the bare kind filler ("grows wheat"), never a universal range.

gaps_confirmed: An adjectivally-restricted bare-plural object in a non-episodic clause ("extinguishes unprotected lanterns"): the prescribed bare kind filler cannot carry the restrictive modifier, and "unprotected" is incidental description (a state, like damage) so *Compound concepts* bars fusing it into `unprotected_lantern`.
new_gaps: A dispositional claim about a SPECIFIC individual's characteristic effect on a KIND has no carrier: the kind-level relation `(<Verb> <kindA> <kindB>)` fires only when BOTH arguments are bare kind-denoting NPs, so a definite singular subject cannot use it, and the plain event route leaves the disposition ("whenever it meets one") unexpressed.
adjudication.defect_summary: The nearest licensed form is the status-less event `(Member sk_ext_1 extinguish) (Agent sk_ext_1 sk_wind_1) (Patient sk_ext_1 lantern)` with no rule — but that silently drops "unprotected", which *Core patterns* forbids because omitting a restriction widens the claim, so NO fully compliant form is licensed for this sentence's content and the claim would have to be left out with the gap recorded.
adjudication.notes: The lexical work is right: the `cold_threshold_wind` genus with the noun modifier unexposed, `Agent` on an inanimate transitive subject, and `Patient` on `extinguish`.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind blows between the first hard frost and the spring equinox.

q1_issues.issue: (Inheritance cold_threshold_wind cold) exposes a genus for half of a NOUN modifier ('cold-threshold' = a threshold of cold): the predication test the modifier-genus rule mandates ('*the wind is cold-threshold') fails, so no modifier genus is licensed, and the emitted atom asserts a coldness of the wind kind the text never predicates.

q2_gaps: 'between <event-noun> and <event-noun>' as an interval frame: Intervals covers only 'from X to / until Y' and its Start/End slots are illustrated with calendar/clock terms, while event-noun temporal anchors are elsewhere routed through Before/BeforeBy ordering — no rule says which applies to 'between A and B'

'the first N' where N is a plain kind noun with no associated event and no explicit '-est' dimension: Ordinal's <scale> slot is defined as 'the associated event, or an explicit -est dimension', neither of which exists here (the parse put the entity's own kind, hard_frost, in the slot)

a three-word hyphenated compound ('cold-threshold wind'): Compound concepts specifies modifier_noun decomposition for a two-part modifier+head only, and is silent on whether a compound modifier is itself unpacked or left whole in the symbol
review.notes: Patient on the wind for 'blows' follows the non-volitional natural-process rule (gases), and the bare simple present correctly takes no status atom. spring_equinox correctly gets its genus and no 'spring' modifier atom (noun modifier), which makes the cold_threshold_wind treatment inconsistent within the same parse.

issues.reason: Compound concepts states 'A noun modifier is never exposed, whatever it names' and gates exposure on the predication test, which 'cold-threshold' fails ('*the wind is cold-threshold'); taking only the modifier's first half yields (Inheritance cold_threshold_wind cold), which predicates a coldness of the wind kind the text never states — the threshold is of cold, not the wind.

gaps_confirmed: 'between <event-noun> and <event-noun>' as an interval frame: Intervals covers 'from X to / until Y' with calendar/clock terms in the Start/End slots, and event-noun anchors are otherwise routed through Before/BeforeBy, with no ruling on 'between A and B'.

'the first N' where N is a plain kind noun with no associated event and no explicit '-est' dimension: the Ordinal <scale> slot is defined as 'the associated event, or an explicit -est dimension', and neither exists here.

A compound modifier inside a fused compound ('cold-threshold wind'): Compound concepts specifies modifier+head decomposition for a single-word modifier and is silent on whether a multi-word modifier is itself unpacked or kept whole in the symbol.
adjudication.defect_summary: The compliant form emits the head genus alone — (Inheritance cold_threshold_wind wind) — leaving 'cold_threshold' unexposed inside the symbol, exactly as the same parse correctly left 'spring' unexposed in spring_equinox; no atom predicating 'cold' of the wind is licensed.
adjudication.notes: The remaining atoms hold: Patient on the wind for 'blows' (non-volitional natural process), the Start/End reading of 'between A and B' and the Ordinal scale improvisation are true and well-typed in the gap territory the reviewer names, and the bare simple present correctly takes no status atom.

fields.sentence: Salt-bloom in mire-essence slows the burn.

q2_gaps: a locative/medium PP restricting the bare-kind SUBJECT of a VERBAL generic ('Salt-bloom in mire-essence slows X'): the instruction set licenses a premise conjunct only for an adjectivally-restricted kind subject, and routes locative restrictions on kind-level claims into ConditionalProperty's condition slot, which has no verbal-generic counterpart — so the encoding of the restriction is unguided
review.notes: Rule route, roles (transitive inanimate subject Agent; occurrence-altering object Patient), decomposition and 0.9/0.9 empirical generic all follow the instruction set. LocatedIn's second slot holds a bare mass kind (mire_essence) rather than a place — mechanically licensed by the containment-preposition rule, but an unusual filler for that head.

fields.sentence: A salt-bloomed lantern survives a cold-threshold night.

q2_gaps: decomposition of a PARTICIPIAL / adjectival compound ("salt-bloomed"): the genus rule is specified for modifier_noun compounds whose last word is a real head noun, and adjective compounds are explicitly told to be left opaque, so nothing licenses or forbids (Inheritance salt_bloomed bloomed)
a compound kind whose MODIFIER is itself multi-word ("cold-threshold night"): "decompose once, to single-word lemmas, then stop" says nothing about the two-word modifier that stays inside the symbol
review.notes: A witness rather than a generic for the indefinite subject is exactly what the Existential section mandates with a verbal predicate, even though the sentence reads as a world rule. Agent/Theme for survive (no possession or stative-psych demotion), splitting the descriptive modifier into its own Member atom, the cold_threshold_night fusion with genus night and no exposed modifier, and the absent status atom all conform.

fields.sentence: An unprepared Cliff Path lantern dies on a cold-threshold night.

q2_gaps: a modified indefinite time NP as a Time filler ('on a cold-threshold night'): the Time section defines structured calendar terms, deictic constants and bare day-part symbols, but gives no form for an indefinite common-noun time NP carrying a restrictive modifier, so an sk_ witness in the Time slot is unlicensed though it is the only reading that does not silently drop 'cold-threshold'
review.notes: The indefinite subject correctly stays a witness rather than a generic (verbal predicate), 'unprepared' correctly stays an adjective-form modifier, and 'Cliff Path' takes the proper-noun-premodifier Possession route with the in-name kind atom.

fields.sentence: The cold-threshold wind does not reach the Northcove.
parse: (: reach_neg (And (Member sk_reach_1 reach) (Agent sk_reach_1 sk_wind_1) (Theme sk_reach_1 northcove)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

review.notes: The definite singular subject stays a witness under negation and its typing correctly projects outside the strength-0 bundle while the event class and roles stay inside; "reach" matches the instruction set's own Agent/Theme example verbatim. Northcove is a coined place name rather than a bare class word, so the Name atom (and the absence of an invented kind atom) is right.
